clue.text: Girl reading articles from opposite points of view?

indicators.note: looking from the other side means seeing things the other way round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the same article again, this time read from the other end

explanation.surface: A girl reads newspaper pieces written from conflicting standpoints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' sounds like newspaper pieces, but it is the grammatical word 'an', taken once each way, so the whole name reads the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a common female first name, and crosswords often clue any given name simply as girl.

clue.text: Chap took a tumble, never mind!

parts.note: fell is the past tense of fall
ah is the shrug of resignation, as in 'ah, never mind'

explanation.surface: A man trips over and someone tells him not to worry about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation stands for the sigh you might say instead of 'never mind', a two-letter interjection.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellah is an informal spelling of fellow or fella, a casual word for a man or bloke.

clue.text: Get emotional when hyacinth, say, pulled up

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulling something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: a hyacinth grows from a bulb; 'say' marks it as one example

explanation.surface: A gardener is upset to find a hyacinth has been yanked out of the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulled up' sounds like weeding, but in a down entry it turns the plant's base upside down. Blub is British slang for crying.
explanation.definitionFit: To blub is to sob or weep, an informal way of being overcome with tearful feeling.

clue.text: Bud is heading for Romania aboard jet

indicators.note: to be aboard is to be inside a vessel, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a jet of water is a spout

indicators.note: a heading is what sits at the top, so only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone named Bud is flying to Romania on a jet plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet' looks like an aircraft to board, but it is a stream of liquid, and 'Bud' is not a person's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprout is a young shoot or bud just beginning to grow from a plant.

clue.text: Like some bacon monk used in a stew

indicators.note: being in a stew means being agitated and jumbled up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A monastery cook throws some bacon into a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used' reads as part of the cooking story, but its letters join the monk's in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is sold either smoked or green, the latter being cured without exposure to wood smoke.

clue.text: Consider when at home, time to cut goatee, say

indicators.note: a cut goes into something, so these pieces are placed inside the other

parts.note: a goatee is one kind of facial hair
being in means being at home
a minute, abbreviated, is a unit of time

explanation.surface: Someone advises that a goatee is best trimmed while relaxing at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goatee, say' marks the goatee as one example of facial hair, and 'when' is only a link; the cut lands just before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something in mind is to keep it in your thoughts and take it into account.

clue.text: Global force in petrol for transportation

indicators.note: transporting moves things from place to place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A worldwide power rests on oil used as fuel for vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition placing the force in fuel; it simply stands first as itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpol is the international police organisation that coordinates law enforcement across many countries.

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its start, so just the opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A celebrated pianist was first carried up on the audience's shoulders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acclaimed' looks like an adjective for the pianist, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclaimed and praised are both past-tense verbs meaning publicly applauded or commended.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who bets, a gambler
second meaning: one who poles a flat-bottomed boat along

explanation.surface: A rower or helmsman is being judged the superior choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as a comparative adjective, but it is one who bets. A punt is a flat boat pushed with a pole, as on the rivers at Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a punter is a gambler, and also someone propelling a punt with a pole.

clue.text: Spanish dish bound to be sent back by the French!

indicators.note: something sent back returns the way it came, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A diner warns that a Spanish dish is certain to be returned to the kitchen by French guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain', but it is the verb meaning to spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Valencian rice dish cooked with saffron, seafood or meat in a wide shallow pan.

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slips' looks like more underwear, as petticoats, but it means errors. A bloomer is British slang for a silly mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers are old-fashioned baggy knickers, and in Britain bloomers are also embarrassing errors.

clue.text: My T-bone steak he cooked as well

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters taken as written, hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: Someone says their partner grilled a T-bone steak for them too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As well' sits at the end like part of the dinner story, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a further point on similar grounds, meaning likewise or also.

clue.text: For example, New York cab driver's initial caution

parts.note: New York taxis are famously painted yellow, an example of a coloured vehicle

indicators.note: an initial is a first letter, so only the start of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A Manhattan taxi driver's first act is to warn the passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' marks the cab as one instance of a colourful vehicle. In football a referee shows a player a card of that colour as a formal warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A booking in football or rugby is a caution, signalled by the referee holding up the card.

explanation.surface: A car is driven in aimless circles.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: one has a long O and two syllables, the other is the past tense of mope.
explanation.definitionFit: A moped is a small motorised bicycle, and moped also means drifted around gloomily and aimlessly.

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A property is described as very nearly luxurious.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the H from the end of the luxurious word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an advantage or benefit, something counting in your favour, like an asset.

indicators.note: beaten things are battered out of shape, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A football wide player curses after being outrun by an opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests football, but its letters join 'as' in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Swearing is the use of profanity, which is exactly what bad or obscene language means.

indicators.note: being involved in something means sitting inside it, so the letters lie within the words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A storage building might play a part in commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the end of 'trade' and the start of 'potentially'.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a storehouse where goods are kept before distribution, much like a warehouse.

indicators.note: something tiresome is troublesome and awkward, so the letters are put into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone sighs about having to drag themselves along to dull parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiresome' looks like a description of the parties, and it also echoes the weariness in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk or trudge somewhere tiredly and reluctantly, often a long way.

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
RIP stands for rest in peace, the farewell on gravestones

explanation.surface: A garden weed has finally been killed off, with a mock farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed' looks like a plant, but in British slang it is a feeble person.
explanation.definitionFit: A drip is a dull, spineless person, and so is a weed in informal British English.

clue.text: Where my ultimate suit was fitted, never!

parts.words: Where my ultimate suit was fitted
parts.note: surface reading: a tailor fitting a last outfit

parts.words: Where my ultimate suit was fitted
parts.note: setter's reading: a burial suit is laid on a corpse

explanation.surface: Someone flatly refuses, thinking of the final suit they will ever wear.
explanation.walkthrough: One's ultimate suit is the one in which one is buried, draped on the corpse; the phrase for its location is an emphatic refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses total refusal, saying something will happen only after the speaker has died.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: inaugural, as of a voyage or speech
second meaning: a young unmarried woman

explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a verb or a failure, but it is the title for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden voyage is a ship's earliest trip, and a maiden is an old word for a young girl.

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its start, so just the opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A brief dip in the tub leaves someone soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' looks like it describes the bath, but it is the definition, meaning mentally sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone quick on the uptake is clever and intelligent, which is what brainy describes.

parts.note: a scar is a blemish, describing the area as scarred
a city is an urban area

explanation.surface: Deprivation is found in a run-down, scarred part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'blemished urban area' is read loosely as a scar city.
explanation.definitionFit: A poverty of something is a shortage of it, so scarcity means lack or insufficiency.

clue.text: Really so boring, ultimately, a system of exercises

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of each word is kept

parts.note: last letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone complains that an exercise routine is truly tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letters of three words are followed by the article, which is also part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga is a Hindu-derived discipline of postures and breathing practised as physical exercise.

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A competitive swimmer is in position on the starting block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person, but it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a flatfish found in European seas, and crosswords often call any fish a swimmer.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a group working together, as on a ship
second meaning: an old past tense of crow, to brag

explanation.surface: A sports side bragged about their win.
explanation.walkthrough: Crew is an older British past tense of crow, as in 'the cock crew'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a group of people working together, and to crow is to brag.

clue.text: Cost with investment of new sovereign

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or install, so one piece is wrapped around another

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A financier counts the cost of investing in a new gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' and 'sovereign' suggest money and coins, but a sovereign is also a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince can be a monarch ruling a principality, so the word can stand for a sovereign.

indicators.note: brewing mixes and steeps ingredients, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Someone makes a drink by brewing it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brewed' fits the drink in the surface, and it is also the signal to mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is an unfermented tea made from unwithered leaves and served as a hot beverage.
